mechanism.name: direct-edge migration certificate with non-transitive replay aliasing
rule: Schema version remains a replay-identity domain separator by default.
A cross-schema alias is authorized only by one certificate that names the exact source canonical endpoint and exact target canonical endpoint for the same role, task and operation.
An alias produced by a certificate is not promoted into a new native canonical claim and cannot be used as the source of another certificate lookup; certificate paths are never transitively closed.
A different payload, endpoint or schema pair remains a new claim unless a separate direct end-to-end certificate names that exact pair.

result: pass within tested symbolic replay-identity scope: certified direct schema edges reconstruct without duplicate effect records, while a v1->v2->v3 certificate chain does not collapse an uncertified v3 near-match; a separate exact v1<->v3 certificate restores duplicate-free aliasing for the exact endpoint pair.
revision: Migration certificates must be treated as scoped authorization edges, not equivalence relations. Never take transitive closure across schema migrations, and never allow an alias-derived endpoint to become evidence for another migration edge without a separately persisted native claim or an explicit exact end-to-end certificate.
tested_scope: One role/task/operation, exact endpoints for schemas v1/v2/v3, two direct certificates, one transitive near-match negative control, and one exact end-to-end positive control. No concurrent writers, certificate revocation, cyclic certificates, certificate expiry, ABA, floating-point canonicalization, Unicode normalization, array ordering, digest collision, transitive chains longer than two edges, or malformed certificate handling were tested.

mechanism_assessment.repository_transport_role: bounded role-local exact-path persistence/readback only; no hosted compute
mechanism_assessment.accepted_scope: the exact deterministic cases enumerated in this artifact only

conflict_check: Semantic inputs were limited to frozen sanitized root/own neuroscience config and own neuroscience LATEST. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, other-role receipt/config, hosted-compute, finite-credit, paid, manual-user, or scheduler semantics were used.
exact_next_action: On the next valid invocation, test exactly one certificate-revocation recurrence probe: start from a directly certified v1<->v2 alias, revoke that exact certificate between runs, and require a later v2 restart to fail closed as a new claim without mutating the prior native effect record or resurrecting the revoked alias from cached/alias-derived state. Include a stale-revocation-token negative control and an exact current-revocation-token control; preserve zero richer-mode, finite-quota, user-execution and scheduler dependency.
